findings.title: Concurrent PUTs to the same key can share a temp file name.
findings.body: The temp file name is `${file}.${process.pid}.${Date.now()}.tmp`. This file-system storage is meant for running the API on a single Node server. On that server, two `PUT`s for the same zip that land in the same millisecond get the same temp path. For example, two CI runs on `shared()` can finish together and both upload `main.zip`. Both requests then write into the same temp file at once, so the zip that gets renamed into place can mix bytes from both bodies. The second `fs.rename` then fails with `ENOENT` because the temp file is already gone, and the client gets a 500. A corrupted `main.zip` makes every later download fail, so every test fails with `IntentStoreError` until someone fixes the bucket. Fix: make the temp name unique per call, for example with `crypto.randomUUID()`.
